The rear top LC5 is 18.2 by 1.9 in with a 0.35 in bevel, and the triangular side LC6 is 8 in deep. All are 0.35 in R45, bonded with micro and glass, 2 plies outside and 1 inside. Keep the left rear console short for the left suitcase. The outlines between the printed corners are fitted shapes.

inside of the sides LC3, LC4 and LC6

Trim-lever hole in LC4 and throttle cutout in LC2

Pieces bonded with micro and glass, 2 plies outside and 1 inside

ops.title: Front thigh support and fuel-valve cover
ops.summary: Cut two ribs 10.8 in long and 3.65 in tall at the front from 0.35 in R45, with a curved top drawn on a sheet this guide does not hold, and notch one for the fuel lines. Cut the floor, 17 by 12.3 in with a 5.6 by 4.5 in notch, heat it to about 280 F and bend it. The ribs stand 5.6 in apart with the fuel valve between. Bond and glass the ribs with one ply, then the floor with one ply inside and two outside, strong enough to stand on. Close the gap under the right console with one more ply. Make the fuel-valve cover from 0.025 in aluminium, 6.6 by 5.0 in, silicone it on with no screws, and mark OFF, LEFT and RIGHT.

ops.title: Canard cover
ops.summary: Fit a block of 2 in green urethane to the canard top and the fuselage, oversize, and tape the fuselage, nose, F28 and elevator slot. Bond it with wet micro to the sanded canard and carve it. Glass the outside with two plies of BID lapping about 1/4 in onto the canard. After the cure remove the canard, hollow the foam, and lay two plies of BID inside with flox corners. The plans print no size beyond the 2 in thickness, so the shape is a fitted outline. After paint seal the joint with a white silicone bead and cure it two to three days before the canard comes off. Not over four man-hours.

inside, on the bare foam, with flox corners

changes.note: Soft sponge rubber at the elevator tubes and RTV at the canard-to-fuselage joint cut the air leak.

completion: Foam block bonded to the sanded canard top and carved
Outside glassed with 2 plies and trimmed

ops.title: Seal between the wing and the centre section
ops.summary: This is the seal that chapter 19 and chapter 23 point to. About half an inch of space separates the wing root from the centre-section spar; the printed fraction cannot be told from 3/4 at this scan resolution. Push urethane foam wedges in with micro on the wing side, let them cure, then sand them to shape and leave 1/16 in at the front. Remove the wing, lay one ply of BID round the foam, and seal the same way along the wing leading-edge and strake gap. After paint fill the small gap with silicone; lay release film on one side if the wings come off often. Air spilling here costs performance and spills engine cooling air.

materials.where: round the foam wedges

completion: Foam wedges bonded in the 1/2 in gap on the wing side
Wedges sanded to shape with 1/16 in left at the front
One ply of BID laid round the foam with the wing off
Silicone fill after paint noted

ops.title: Inspect the structure and make the sanding spline
ops.summary: Make a 9 by 9 in sanding spline from four to six BID plies laid over waxed paper, with a foam pad and two handles. Then inspect and repair every structure before any filler goes on. A dip or hump over 1/16 in across more than 20 percent of the local chord needs a repair, and a 12 in ruler laid on the skin shows it. The holes and voids found here take the coarse fill in the next step. Work in a shop at 70 F or above. The finish colours are decided now, because the glass resin must stay under its softening temperature of 160 F and the surface of a black airplane on a hot day approaches 220 F.

changes.note: Check the surface contour with a feeler gauge: a gap over 0.006 in under a straightedge is too wavy.

completion: Sanding spline made
Every structure inspected, dips and humps over 1/16 in over 20 percent of the chord repaired
Shop held at 70 F or above
Colours chosen with the 160 F resin limit in mind

ops.title: Coarse fill
ops.summary: Hand-sand the voids, tack-coat with epoxy and lump on dry micro, never Bondo, which is four times as heavy. Fill depth sets the method; under 0.03 in takes feather fill later, 0.03 to 0.20 in takes dry micro, and over 0.20 in takes a block of urethane foam with one or two plies of BID. Wait a full day at minimum before sanding the micro to contour with 36 to 60 grit and a hard block. The plans text prints 35 to 60 once and the sketch 36 to 60; this guide takes the sketch. Sand into the first skin ply only, in local spots up to 2 in across, under 5 percent of the surface.

changes.note: Dry micro weighs about 3 lb per gallon, Bondo about 12; use dry micro.

completion: Voids sanded and tack-coated, dry micro lumped on where 0.03 to 0.20 in deep
Foam block and glass over any depth beyond 0.20 in
Micro cured 24 hours and sanded to contour with 36 to 60 grit
Skin sand-through kept under 5 percent of the surface

ops.title: Feather fill
ops.summary: Brush feather fill, with about 25 percent micro-balloons by volume, over the glass to 0.02 to 0.03 in, in a shop at 70 F or above, then sand it with 100 grit and a soft block. Over 95 percent of what goes on comes off as dust, so the finished layer is far thinner than the wet one. The glass weave is 0.009 in rough, which this layer buries. A later Canard Pusher bulletin gives 25 to 50 percent micro-balloons and a 1.5 gal cap for a VariEze, a ratio that differs from this page and is carried here as a conflict. Never put feather fill over primer.

changes.note: Fog coat, 25 to 50 percent micro-balloons, 100 grit, two or three coats; this is a VariEze bulletin and differs from the plans ratio.

completion: Feather fill brushed on at 70 F or above
Layer sanded with 100 grit to 0.02 to 0.03 in
Weave texture buried

ops.title: Primer
ops.summary: Spray two coats of dark grey lacquer primer, built to 0.004 to 0.008 in, over the sanded feather fill. Sand with 220 grit and then wet with 320. The plans name the Dupont 70S, 100S and 3011S; a later bulletin says 131S replaces the discontinued 100S. The cockpit gets one primer coat and no fill, with the nose-gear window and the fuel gauges masked first. In the lab the whole airplane goes primer grey here, which is a representational colour.

changes.note: Dupont 131S replaces the discontinued 100S primer; keep one maker's system.

completion: Two coats of primer sprayed to 0.004 to 0.008 in
Sanded with 220 grit, then wet 320
Cockpit primed once, nose-gear window and gauges masked

ops.title: Paint, seals and marks
ops.summary: Spray the finish coat. The rule is white only on the upper wing and canard, with no dark trim there and no stripe except at the canard tip; white absorbs about 10 percent of the sun and black about 95. Trim is allowed on the fuselage, the vertical winglet surfaces and the undersides. After the cure seal the gaps with white silicone and wait two days before any part is separated. No finish weight is printed. The N26MS parts weighed before and after finish give about +1.0 lb on the canopy, +0.275 lb on each aileron and +2.2 lb on each wing, as references only; the whole airplane's finish was never weighed. Then the N-numbers.

changes.note: White paint keeps the glass resin cool; a red stripe ran about 50 F hotter than the adjacent white.

completion: Finish coat sprayed, white on the upper wing and canard only
Gaps sealed with white silicone and cured two days before parts come apart
N-numbers applied
Finish weight recorded as not printed, with the N26MS deltas as references

ops.title: Cushions and headrests
ops.summary: The front cushion is 46 by 16.5 in in plan and 2 in of foam rubber under a fabric cover; its notch reads 6 to 8 in by 6 in and which is which is a guess. The rear seat cushion is 12 in deep and 16 in wide with a back 18 in tall, from 2 in blocks, 4 in high at the front edge. The front headrest is 4.5 by 4.5 by 2 in, bonded to the rollover with contact cement; the rear one is 4.5 by 4.5 by 1.5 in, held by two snapped flaps over the canopy braces. The front seat fits a pilot from 6 ft 3 in to 6 ft 5 in, and a smaller pilot adds cushion. Paint the interior first. No weight is printed, and the later weight-creep warning in the newsletter is only an example.
completion: Interior painted before any upholstery goes in
Front and rear cushions laid on the seat floors
Front headrest cemented to the rollover, rear headrest snapped over the canopy braces

ops.title: Suitcases
ops.summary: Each suitcase is 30 in on the long edge, 18 in high at the rear edge, 14 in across the top and 5 in thick full (4.5 in collapsed, a small read). The shell is ABS plastic 0.06 to 0.09 in thick or four plies of BID, with a fabric bag held by snaps every 4 in and a stiffener leg 15 in long. The left one is shortened to clear the landing brake; the cut length is not printed. Two inserts for the unused rear area hold the map cases, the ELT and a survival kit. The shape between the dimensions is a fitted outline. This is the last page of the plans.

materials.where: suitcase shell, if not ABS plastic

completion: Two suitcases made or bought to the printed sizes
Left suitcase shortened to clear the landing brake
Short-pilot inserts made if wanted
